tag: Episode 28 Side Story · The First to Recognize Her
title: The First to Recognize Her

beats.t: The next morning, Yeoni opened their notes and read each line aloud.
One, black umbrella even on clear days. Two, rain smell in clear weather. Name: Seo Hanbi, cold rain.
Three, saying giving a name creates a debt. Four, saying a debt grows if left alone.
(Five, ring mark on right wrist. Six, habit of stopping before someone hurt.)
Yeoni pointed to the next line. Seven, Neo wary of her right wrist. Stepped in front of me the instant he saw her.
“Eight, asked the price when you shared an umbrella.”
I was about to write that. No spoilers from Customer Support.
Then Yeoni remembered. The Library of Resources. The chase between shelves. The name stitched inside the fluttering black cloak. The drumming child's name.
(That tiger stopped before a hurt child, too. Didn't know what to do when given bread.)
Seo Hanbi is that tiger. The black tiger.
“...Yes. I remember now, too. That smell. Upriver.”
But why is that tiger living next door? As a human?
“One of two reasons. To hunt you, or protect you.”
(She wrote not to go to the bus stop on the card. Would someone hunting me write that?)
Then I'll ask. She's next door.
“Dangerous. Over there, she hunted you. She still has claws here.”
I know. But I saw her cry at the stop. Hunters don't cry like that.
“...Your judgment of people has improved. Thanks to Customer Support's training.”
Thanks to Luna's sister's bread. I saw a lot of people while eating bread.
At the door, Yeoni's hands shook while tying their sneakers. Neo crouched beside them and held the loose knot.
“I'm coming. Don't stop me if I hiss.”
Yeoni stood before the neighbor's door, empty-handed. Maybe they should have brought bread.
Three knocks. After a long wait, the door opened a little. Seo Hanbi's eyes appeared through the chained gap.
What is it? It's early.
I've come for my umbrella. And to ask something.
The taped umbrella emerged through the gap. Yeoni did not take it. Instead, they called softly through the door.
Ms. Tiger?
The umbrella fell. Tap. The sound alone echoed through the corridor.
...Wrong apartment.
Do you still have the drumming child's name? In your coat's inner pocket?
Without knowing it, Seo Hanbi's hand went to her chest. Then stopped. Too late.
It's there. Thank goodness.
Color drained from her face. Beyond the chain, she steadied her breathing. The door did not close.
I can't remember that child's name. Things blurred after I came here. But you still have it.
I tried to throw it away. So many times. It would clear the ledger. But I couldn't.
How... Everything blurs here. You weren't supposed to know anything.
I wrote it down. Afraid I'd forget. Everything you let slip.
Then you know what I did to you. Who collected all your fortune.
I know. That's why I came to ask. Why move next door? To finish it, or to protect me?
Seo Hanbi couldn't answer. Beyond the chain, her lips opened and closed twice.
Both. Ordered to finish it. Wanted to protect you. Managed neither.
Is that why you stood with an umbrella every clear day? Guarding my door?
When rain comes, it comes. Where there's water. That's why I told you not to go to the stop on rainy days.
What comes?
Instead of an answer, Yeoni's phone lit up in their pocket. A pitch-black screen. A black circle at its center. A sun burning red only at the rim.
Black hands reached from the screen. One, two, twelve. They wrapped around Yeoni's wrists and ankles.
These... those hands from over there! But this is reality!
Too late, hound. I told you to finish it there. I'll collect in person.
No! That child isn't empty yet!
Then empty it. Open the door. With your own hands this time.
The hands dragged Yeoni toward the phone. The screen widened into a door. Unfamiliar stars swirled beyond.
Seo Hanbi tore off the chain. The door flew open. At her right wrist, the gold cord burned red.
The black coat became fur. Hands became paws, nails claws. A black tiger filled the corridor, standing before Yeoni.
Get your hands off that child.
One sweep severed three hands. They grew back. The tiger cut again. The golden ring on its right forepaw dug into flesh.
Disobeying again. Have you forgotten whose ring that is?
I haven't. That's why I'm repaying it myself this time.
The tiger covered Yeoni with its body. This time, the hands wrapped around the tiger instead.
Ms. Tiger! Let go. Let's hold on together!
Thank you for the umbrella. I'll put that in the ledger. As uncollected.
The hands dragged the tiger into the screen. The tip of its black tail brushed Yeoni's hand last. Like cold rainwater.
The corridor went quiet. The fluorescent light flickered once, then came back on.
On the floor remained a taped umbrella and one wet pawprint. A red pawprint.
I called her. I recognized her, and that's why...
Neo knelt before Yeoni. He offered his hand but waited until they took it. His gaze still faced the corridor's end.
“Not your fault. Because you recognized her first, she chose with her own hands. Perhaps for the first time.”
[ Another sky has opened · The Twelve Palaces ]
The app opened on the phone by itself. Like the day Yeoni first installed it, only one button appeared.
Nobody's making me press it this time. I'll press it myself.
Yeoni picked up the umbrella. Its taped handle was still warm from Seo Hanbi holding it for so long.
I have to return this. I'm going to bring her back. This time, she's not getting away for free.
Inside the wallet, Yundal's talisman began glowing warmly. Over the folded paper, a crescent slowly waxed.
